Landscape 4:3 research artwork CLAY TESTING for an early civilization game. Match reference aesthetic only: flat dry matte gouache, warm opaque ivory paper, charcoal, ochre, gray-sage, restrained grain and irregular vignette edges; not a photograph. Close oblique overhead study of hands comparing fired clay test pieces on a reed mat. Five little plain test tiles and two pinched test cups: one tile deeply cracked from shrinkage, one warped, one crumbly coarse-grained, two sound with subtly different clay colors. One ordinary weathered hand lifts a broken tile so its coarse cross-section is visible; the other points at a shrinkage crack. Small raw clay lumps and a pinch of sand nearby. THIS IS MATERIAL TESTING, not decorative pottery-making: no potter wheel, finished ornate vessels, writing, numbers, modern measuring equipment, metal tools or laboratory glass. Hands belong to seated workers partly visible along upper edge in simple invented early woven wraps. No posed faces or glamour. Main test pieces and gestures all fit compact central horizontal band; ample paper margins. Strongly distinguish the different results through cracks, shape and texture rather than labels. No UI, text or border.
